attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post. The Libin quote that follows is not part of the claim.

semantics.note: Revision 2 restores 'can be buggy' and the 'astonishing in familiar cases' point. The firm part is 'highly dependent on similarity'; the 'can be' parts are weak possibility statements.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair: high dependence needs evidence tying familiarity to correctness, kept apart from difficulty. The 2025-to-post window is a reasonable reading of the present-tense claim.

evidence.note: A June 2025 benchmark with contamination-reduced problems shows failures on hard problems. That fits the 'can be buggy' part, but difficulty is not separated from familiarity and actual training exposure is not measured.

A Sept 2025 revision finds memorization that depends on the task and declines on simple tasks. Its experiments come after the target window, and the picture is qualified, so it does not settle the July observation.

reviews.rationale: The weak 'can be buggy' part fits e1, but the firm claim of high dependence on training similarity needs controlled familiarity tests. The packet has none from the window: e1 mixes novelty with difficulty, and e2 is later and mixed. So the evidence does not settle it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The causal 'because' is kept. Folding 'very little has been discussed explicitly' into 'company secrecy' is a slight compression but faithful.

contract.note: The plain reading (withheld methods substantially reduced public neurosymbolic knowledge) is ordinary. It invents no thresholds and requires evidence that withholding caused the loss.

evidence.note: The 2024 FMTI documents broad opacity but also improving transparency. It is not specific to neurosymbolic work and does not measure lost research.
The Feb 2025 AlphaGeometry2 paper is one detailed company disclosure of a neurosymbolic system. It cannot establish the overall disclosure rate or the size of any research loss.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows general opacity and one counterexample of detailed disclosure. It has no inventory of withheld neurosymbolic methods and no measure of research lost because of secrecy, so the causal claim is neither shown nor refuted.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'far better on some tasks but not all' and the hallucination comparison. Leaving out 'effective for some tasks, but not others' is a minor, largely redundant omission.

contract.note: Reading 'far better' as a substantial advantage on some tasks, and 'worse on hallucinations' as higher measured hallucination rates, is ordinary and fair.

evidence.note: The system card (a company disclosure) reports o3 hallucination rates above o1's: 0.33 vs 0.16 on PersonQA and 0.51 vs 0.44 on SimpleQA. o3 accuracy is also higher.
The launch post (a company disclosure) reports new SOTA on several benchmarks and large gains from tool use on AIME. This supports substantial advantages on some tasks.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's own release evaluations show o3 hallucinating more than o1 on both fact-seeking tests, and large tool-enabled gains on some tasks with only marginal gains on others (e.g. SimpleQA accuracy). The sources are company disclosures, but they are the primary benchmark records the contract names.

attribution.note: Marcus's own conclusion in his own post.

semantics.note: 'We can safely conclude ... on track to be' is firm, unhedged language about a future outcome, so it is a forecast. No deadline is given.

contract.note: 'Major part' is undefined. Reading it as sustained, widespread use across leading systems is a fair ordinary reading, but the result depends on that threshold. The contract rightly refuses to count non-adoption by a chosen date as failure.

evidence.note: A Sept 2025 Anthropic disclosure that Claude runs code to create files. Consistent with the forecast, but it covers one provider and has no field-wide measure.
A May 2026 Anthropic platform launch that includes code execution. It shows availability, not a dated assessment of widespread sustained use.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, and the early-resolution rule needs a dated deployment assessment of widespread sustained use. The packet has only single-provider product launches, so the forecast is still open.
